problem:
Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the following two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+3z-11=0 \\ 2x-2y-5=0\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
First, we notice:

- For the plane $2x+3z-11=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨2,0,3⟩.$

- For the plane $2x-2y-5=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨2,-2,0⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨2,0,3⟩\times ⟨2,-2,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =6i+6j-4k \\  & =⟨6,6,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$
